title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Palladium on 1972-09-10
lineage: SBD> MR> Cassette> DAT> CD> EAC> CoolEdit2000> SHN

ai_review.summary: Clear sound‑board tape captures a high‑energy September 1972 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star, soaring Birdsong and a killer Playin'.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid sound‑board source with generally clear balance and only occasional patch‑ups or minor drop‑outs. Musically the performance is vibrant – Jerry’s tone and soloing are praised throughout, Phil delivers several “bombs,” and the setlist rolls from a standout Playin' into an epic Dark Star that flows into Jack Straw, with Birdsong, Black Peter and Truckin' also getting high marks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and highlight strong musical moments; recording quality is consistently described as good/acceptable with only minor issues, yielding a combined rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and warm early‑70s SBD sound; occasional patches are seamless, minor tape glitch noted around 0:57 of Greatest Story, a few short cuts but overall acceptable with no major drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical 1972 two‑set flow with a solid first set and a second set built around an expansive Dark Star > Jack Straw sequence; transitions are praised as tight and the energy builds throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone described as massive, perfect, chunky and “Coltrane‑like” soloing on Playin' and Dark Star; his vocal embellishments noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is highlighted for powerful bass “bombs,” a spotlight solo in Dark Star, and interesting fills throughout the jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir receives praise for harmony work (Birdsong, Casey Jones) and creative guitar moments, though occasional tuning/harmony issues are mentioned.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux noted leading charge in later Dark Star sections and delivering notable phasing; overall keyboard texture appreciated.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is described as “outer planets,” with strong groove work on Playin' and other jams.
